digest.component_or_area: parent-child cascade table and lifecycle concurrency guarantees
propositions: The _CASCADING_EDGES table's one-eligible-status-per-edge shape permits two reachable residuals that do not cascade: reactivating a closed child under an open parent, and blocked→in_progress resume under an open parent.

The documented invariant 'no non-terminal-state ticket can be a child of a closed ticket' is maintained jointly by the table's two closed-source rows and the unconditional open-children close guard in transition_close.py.
The §I4a headline overstates the cascade guarantee; it must be narrowed from 'a child never runs ahead of its parent' to the per-edge same-edge guarantee the table actually provides.
The blocked→in_progress resume fires on the start-work gate but does not cascade; both gate-fire and non-cascade are consistent when documented together since they answer different questions.

The enumerated-table design (retaining AC1's decision) enforces the operator-ruled invariant without requiring a total status-ordering predicate, which would contradict the documented residual that an in_progress child under an open parent is permissible.
